about_p1: The Pakarina spatiotemporal platform was established in 2026 through the collaborative work of professors from the Federal University of Ouro Preto (UFOP), the State University of Minas Gerais (UEMG), Fiocruz Minas, and the National University of San Cristóbal de Huamanga (Peru). The initiative also includes the participation of international exchange students from the Catholic University of Salta (Argentina), ISEN Yncréa Ouest (France), and Benin, a country located on the African continent.
about_p2: The platform aims to georeference arbovirus occurrences and to bring together information, tools, devices, and people that currently operate in separate environments, recognizing that the dynamics of these diseases are determined by a set of interconnected processes involving climatic, urban, environmental, and social factors.
about_p3: Climate variability influences the abundance and competence of disease vectors, while unplanned urbanization and inadequate sanitation systems increase human-vector contact. In addition, human mobility and environmental changes contribute to the spatial spread of infectious agents and to modifications in vector habitats.
about_p4: In this context, the One Health approach integrates human, animal, and environmental dimensions, highlighting that arboviruses circulate within complex and dynamic ecological networks, often involving enzootic cycles before transmission to human populations.
about_p5: Major urban arboviral diseases such as dengue, chikungunya, and Zika illustrate this complexity, as their transmission is predominantly associated with Aedes aegypti and Aedes albopictus mosquitoes. From a clinical perspective, these diseases can range from mild symptoms to severe and potentially fatal outcomes.
about_p6: More recently, the Oropouche virus has attracted increasing attention due to its rapid geographic expansion across the Americas. Its transmission is mainly associated with the biting midge Culicoides paraensis, creating particularly complex epidemiological and ecological challenges for the surveillance and control of this emerging arboviral disease.
about_p7: At its core, Pakarina is developing a modern web platform capable of integrating information from sensors, monitoring devices, databases, mapping systems, external services, and educational resources, designed as a scalable and adaptable foundation.
about_p8: Our vision is to build a sustainable technological ecosystem that strengthens monitoring capabilities, improves information accessibility, and promotes collaboration between technical and non-technical stakeholders, connecting people, information, and action.

home_module_news: Stay informed with the latest epidemiological news on dengue, automatically collected from over 20 trusted media sources across Brazil, Argentina, Peru, France, and beyond. Filter by country, source, or date to follow what matters most.
home_module_climate: Visualize real-time weather conditions and understand how temperature, humidity, and rainfall influence dengue mosquito proliferation. Climate data is combined with environmental analysis to provide actionable risk insights.
home_module_awareness: Access educational resources, prevention guides, and awareness campaigns related to dengue. This module supports communities, schools, and institutions with clear and accessible public health information.
home_module_dashboard: Monitor the platform's key indicators through an integrated dashboard. Currently displaying live weather data for João Monlevade, the dashboard will progressively integrate sensor data, maps, and real-time alerts in future sprints.
home_hero_text: A centralized platform for dengue monitoring, data integration, and community awareness — developed at UFOP.
home_dengue_title: Dengue in Brazil — A Growing Crisis
home_dengue_text: Brazil is the country most affected by dengue in the world. In 2024, over 10 million cases were recorded — a historic record — along with nearly 6,000 deaths. The disease spreads through the Aedes aegypti mosquito and thrives in warm, humid conditions, making monitoring and prevention more critical than ever.
home_stat_source: Sources: Brazilian Ministry of Health, PAHO — 2024 data
home_summary_text: Pakarina is an interdisciplinary initiative developed at the Federal University of Ouro Preto (UFOP) in partnership with UCASAL and Yncrea. It centralizes fragmented data sources related to dengue into a single, unified web platform — improving coordination between technical teams, researchers, educators, and public health institutions.
home_mission_text: Pakarina aims to build a sustainable technological ecosystem that strengthens monitoring capabilities, improves information accessibility, and promotes collaboration between technical and non-technical participants. By combining technology, research, and community engagement, Pakarina seeks to create tools that contribute to public health, environmental awareness, and innovation-driven problem solving.
